Daleszyce Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Daleszyce, Poland

Demolished. Daleszyce's Jews were forbidden to settle or buy houses until the mid-18th century; even afterward, Catholic residents attacked their permanent settlement with blood libel accusations in 1819, 1847, and 1855, driven partly by trade competition. An independent Jewish community was only established in 1869, growing to 525 people by 1937; in September 1942, almost the entire community was deported to the Bodzentyn Ghetto, documented elsewhere in this collection, and then to Treblinka. This cemetery, established next to the Catholic cholera cemetery in the first half of the 19th century, likely began as an epidemic burial ground around 1823 before becoming a regular cemetery.
